# Standard table styler: blue italic title row + palegreen column header row.
# Defined here so all QMDs that source this setup get the same presentation
# without depending on census_helpers.R for a purely cosmetic function.
ds_style_flextable <- function(ft, title = NULL) {
  if (!base::is.null(title)) {
    ft <- flextable::add_header_lines(ft, values = title)
    ft <- flextable::color(ft, i = 1, part = "header", color = "blue")
    ft <- flextable::italic(ft, i = 1, part = "header")
    ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 1, part = "header", align = "left")
    ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, i = 1, part = "header", size = 12)
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, i = 1, part = "header", bg = "white")
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, i = 2, part = "header", bg = "palegreen")
  } else {
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, i = 1, part = "header", bg = "palegreen")
  }
  ft <- flextable::autofit(ft)
  ft
}

## 3-minute speech

Mayor and Council,

My name is Dan Swart, I live at 1509 Gwendolyn Way, Schertz 78154, and I am asking you to slow down before approving the personnel parts of this budget.



The budget says staff compensation is needed to reduce turnover and attract the best talent. It also says more staffing is needed to provide service, prevent burnout, lower EMS response times, support Fire Station 4, and increase drainage maintenance.^[City of Schertz, *FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget*, pp. 6-9.]

But where is the hard evidence?

Where is the position-by-position proof showing which jobs are truly hard to fill?
Where is the data on how many qualified applicants applied?
How many first offers were turned down?
How many employees actually left for another city?
How many vacancies were caused by pay, and how many were caused by management, scheduling, hiring delays, or jobs that may not even need to continue?

The budget asks for a citywide merit and step program that costs $784,000, and it adds 26 positions across several funds.^[City of Schertz, *FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget*, pp. 7-8.]
That is a serious long-term commitment.
And this is being proposed while the General Fund still shows an operating shortfall, while Water and Sewer shows a shortfall, and while Drainage still shows a shortfall even after a major fee increase.^[City of Schertz, *FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget*, pp. 14-16.]

So the first question should not be, “Would higher pay help?”
The first question should be five simple words:

**If we can afford it.**

Compensation should be handled with laser-like accuracy, not a shotgun approach.
If there are three or four positions that are truly hard to fill, then deal with those three or four positions.
Do not use a broad pay approach when the actual problem may be narrow.
And before raising pay for any position, first prove that the position should continue to exist at all.
A vacancy is not always a problem. Sometimes it is a warning sign that the job should be redesigned, combined, delayed, or discontinued.

And please do not confuse better hiring statistics with better government.
Higher pay may attract more applicants.
Higher pay may improve retention.
But that does not prove better judgment, better work ethic, better service, or better results.
It may simply produce a more expensive payroll that taxpayers must carry year after year.

That is why I ask you to require local evidence before voting yes.
Not slogans.
Not assumptions.
Not vague talk about “meeting the market.”

Require proof for each position:
Is the job necessary?
Is there a real local hiring problem?
Is pay truly the cause?
What is the smallest effective fix?
And can the City afford the long-term cost?

That is the standard taxpayers deserve.

Thank you.

## Source note

This speech is based on the City of Schertz FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget, especially the Message and Highlights, Executive Summary, and fund summaries.^[City of Schertz, *FY 2025-26 Proposed Budget*, pp. 5-16.]
